name: adv_gnn_bad
title: PyTorch Geometric node classification and link prediction - nine planted defects
origin: the defective twin of adv_gnn_clean, hardening round 1, 2026-09-13
note: The two graph-specific leaks (the training loss reading test_mask, and message passing over the held-out edges) have no rule in the catalog: MLV101/MLV102 model an sklearn transformer fitted on the wrong rows, not a boolean mask selecting them. They are recorded under `unsupported`.

expected.defect: F.softmax at line 42 feeds F.cross_entropy at line 45, which log-softmaxes it a second time
expected.why: the gradient is flattened towards zero and the model trains far slower than the loss curve suggests; the one subscript between the two (`probabilities[data.test_mask]`) is the only thing between this and MLV401's documented SSA chain walk
the GCN carries nn.Dropout(0.5), so half the hidden units are dropped while accuracy is measured and every reported number is noisy

expected.defect: evaluate() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad() and carries no decorator
expected.why: a full autograd graph over the whole graph is built 200 times and discarded

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path and breaks when the file moves

expected.defect: neither file seeds torch, numpy or random
expected.why: the dropout masks, the parameter init and RandomLinkSplit's partition all move between runs

expected.defect: accuracy is computed on raw logits rather than on argmax classes
expected.why: accuracy_score compares a float matrix against integer labels, so the reported accuracy is meaningless (and on a real run it raises rather than lying, which is the only mercy here)

expected.defect: decode() returns torch.sigmoid(score) at line 43 and the loss is BCEWithLogitsLoss, which sigmoids again
expected.why: the effective gradient is squashed twice, so the model barely learns; the sigmoid sits behind one module-local helper, which is the only thing between this and MLV402's documented final-op chain walk

forbidden.why: the order is zero_grad (38) -> backward (46) -> step (47)
the only no_grad here is the @torch.no_grad() decorator on evaluate(); loss.backward() is in train_epoch()
nothing accumulates a loss across iterations - train_epoch returns float(loss.item())
link_pred.evaluate() calls model.eval() at line 75 and train_epoch() calls model.train() at line 47
link_pred.evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator at line 73
there is no cross-entropy loss in link_pred.py
there is no binary cross-entropy in node_clf.py
data is moved to DEVICE once at line 65; full-batch transductive training has no per-batch tensor to move
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 18
GCN.__init__ calls super().__init__() on its first line
conv1, conv2 and dropout are plain attributes, which nn.Module registers
there is no DataLoader in this project - both trainers are full-batch
there is no DataLoader in this project

unsupported.defect: the training loss is computed on the test mask, so the held-out split is trained on
unsupported.why: MLV101 and MLV102 are about an sklearn transformer fitted on the wrong rows. A boolean mask selecting the test nodes for a torch loss is the same leak in a different idiom and no rule models it. This is the single highest-severity defect in the program and MLView says nothing.

unsupported.defect: the checkpoint is selected on the test mask over 200 epochs
unsupported.why: MLV107 (test set used for model selection or early stopping) is a later-tier rule that has not been built.

unsupported.defect: message passing runs over the complete edge index, so the encoder propagates along the very edges it is asked to predict
unsupported.why: no rule models graph-structural leakage through the message-passing edge set.

unsupported.defect: negative sampling is given the training edges only, so held-out positive edges are drawn as negatives and labelled 0
unsupported.why: no rule models negative-sampling exclusion sets.

unsupported.defect: the ranking metric is fed thresholded hard labels instead of scores
unsupported.why: MLV306's documented detection is `a score argument bound to <clf>.predict(...)`; a threshold comparison on a tensor is a different shape and the rule does not reach it.
